<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Qwen3.5's dense MLP runs SiLU*mul and the NVFP4 quantization of the down_proj input as one FlashInfer kernel. Qwen3 uses `Qwen2MLP`, which lacks that path, so its NVFP4 W4A4 MLPs write the activation in 16 bits (`act_and_mul`) and read it back (`fp4_quantize`).

## Modifications

- Move the fused call and its enabling check from `Qwen2MoeMLP` / `qwen3_5.py` to `models/utils.py` and give `Qwen2MLP` the same branch, enabled only by `Qwen3DecoderLayer` when both projections use ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A4. Other `Qwen2MLP` users are unchanged.
- Keep it off where down_proj cannot use the fused output. Qwen3.5's dense MLP shares these checks, so it gets them too.
  - NVFP4 AWQ: the fused kernel skips `pre_quant_scale` (#38864 adds the same check to the Qwen3.5 copy).
  - The Marlin FP4 GEMM backend, the default on SM80-SM90: it takes a floating-point input.
  - A down_proj K that is not a multiple of 64: the fused kernel leaves the padded scale columns unwritten.
  - Per forward, sequence parallelism or a LoRA-wrapped down_proj: both read the activation tensor (as `DualGemm.can_run` does). Without the LoRA check, a Qwen3 NVFP4 server with a down_proj adapter fails at startup.
- CPU unit tests for each gate, and that the fusion turns on for W4A4.

## Accuracy Tests

- The fused FP4 data and block scales are bit-identical to the two-kernel path (M = 128 to 40960, intermediate size 9728).
- `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` NVFP4 on 60 questions each of Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko: Recall@10 0.876 / 0.767 and the distance to BF16 scores are identical to main.
- `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` NVFP4 as a causal LM (CUDA graphs on), and `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` NVFP4 with a down_proj LoRA adapter: greedy outputs match main.
- On an L4 (SM89, `auto` picks Marlin), greedy outputs and logprobs match main (`Qwen3-Reranker` 0.6B and 4B NVFP4).
- `test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py`: 15 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), FlashInfer 0.7.1. `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` NVFP4, GPU time of one `encode` call on 128 sequences:

| 128 sequences | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 320 tokens | 455.6 ms | **419.0 ms** (-8.0%) |
| 640 tokens | 925.1 ms | **844.2 ms** (-8.7%) |

Decode throughput of `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` NVFP4 at batch 1 / 16 / 64 is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>The kernels alone (CUPTI, cold L2), SiLU*mul + NVFP4 quantization of a [M, 2 x 9728] BF16 input</summary>

| M | `silu_and_mul` + `fp4_quantize` | fused |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 28.4 us | 9.4 us |
| 8192 | 444.1 us | 249.9 us |
| 40960 | 2294.8 us | 1251.9 us |

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

nodes.body: @Fridge003 @ishandhanani @Qiaolin-Yu Could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have a moment? It shares Qwen3.5's dense-MLP SiLU+NVFP4 fusion with Qwen3 (models/ has no CODEOWNERS entry, so no reviewer was requested). Thanks!
Rebased onto the latest main so CI can run. Gentle ping @Fridge003 in case this got buried. Thanks!

Rebased onto main. #45219 added a block-FP8 decode fusion to the same branch of `Qwen2MLP.forward`; the two apply to different quantization methods, so both are kept. @BBuf, since you reviewed #45219, could you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have a moment? Thanks!
[BBuf Review Agent] One thing to fix before this can go in.

[BBuf Review Agent] Qwen3 NVFP4 with `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin` now sends an FP4 tuple to `apply_fp4_marlin_linear`, which requires a floating-point tensor, so the first forward crashes. Could we exclude Marlin in the shared enabling check and cover this MLP handoff?

@BBuf 
Thanks!
On SM80-SM90 `auto` also picks Marlin, so this would have broken the default path there. f5c2129d keeps the fusion off on the Marlin backend. Qwen3.5's dense MLP uses the same check, so it's covered too, and `test_stays_off_for_the_marlin_backend` fails without the change.

Checked with Qwen3-Reranker NVFP4 checkpoints:
- L4 (SM89, `auto` picks Marlin): the previous head failed on the first forward. Greedy outputs and logprobs now match main exactly (0.6B and 4B).
- RTX PRO 6000 with `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`: the previous head failed with `'tuple' object has no attribute 'dtype'`. It now serves normally.
- RTX PRO 6000 with the default backend: the fusion stays on, and outputs match main exactly.

While re-checking the handoff I found one more case. When down_proj's K is not a multiple of 64, the FP4 scales are padded, and the fused kernel leaves the padding unwritten (fp4_quantize zeroes it). In a kernel test with K = 1376 and 608, a NaN byte left there turned the whole GEMM output into NaN. 47dcb3e4 keeps the fusion off for such K; every Qwen3 size at TP <= 8 is a multiple of 64. 8b512342 moves the kill switch into `Envs` and logs the enable message once.
[BBuf Review Agent] The shared guard now excludes Marlin for both Qwen3 and Qwen3.5, and the regression test covers that check. This addresses the tuple handoff crash.

+    try:
+        from flashinfer import silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return
+    mlp._enable_silu_fp4_quant_fusion = True
+    mlp.down_proj._accepts_prequantized_fp4 = True
+    print_info_once("Enabled fused SiLU+mul+FP4-quant for dense MLP down_proj input.")
+
+
+def can_run_silu_fp4_quant_fusion(
+    mlp: torch.nn.Module, gate_up: torch.Tensor | tuple
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether this forward can hand down_proj the fused (fp4, scale) tuple."""
+    return (
+        mlp._enable_silu_fp4_quant_fusion
+        and not isinstance(gate_up, tuple)
+        and not get_forward().sp_active  # the SP g-bar matmul needs a tensor
+        and not hasattr(mlp.down_proj, "base_layer")  # LoRA reads the activation
+    )
+
+
+def silu_and_mul_fp4_quant(
+    mlp: torch.nn.Module, gate_up: torch.Tensor
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """SiLU(gate) * up of a dense MLP, quantized to NVFP4 for its down_proj."""
+    from flashinfer import silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize
+
+    # input_scale_inv only exists after weight loading, so derive it lazily;
+    # the fused kernel requires a 1-D global scale.
+    if mlp._down_input_scale_inv_1d is None:
+        mlp._down_input_scale_inv_1d = mlp.down_proj.input_scale_inv.reshape(1)
+    num_tokens = gate_up.shape[0]
+    masked_m = mlp._masked_m_cache.get(num_tokens)
+    if masked_m is None:
+        masked_m = torch.tensor([num_tokens], dtype=torch.int32, device=gate_up.device)
+        mlp._masked_m_cache[num_tokens] = masked_m
+    y_fp4, y_sf = silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize(
+        gate_up.unsqueeze(0),
+        masked_m,
+        mlp._down_input_scale_inv_1d,
+    )
+    # [M, K/2, 1] -> [M, K/2]; scale: expert-grouped 6-D swizzle
+    # (32, 4, m_blocks, 4, K/64, 1) -> the dense swizzled layout
+    # fp4_gemm expects (verified bit-exact vs fp4_quantize up to FP4
+    # rounding ties for M in 64..8192).
+    y_fp4 = y_fp4.squeeze(-1).view(torch.uint8)
+    m_padded = y_sf.shape[2] * y_sf.shape[0] * y_sf.shape[3]  # m_blocks*32*4
+    y_sf = y_sf.view(torch.uint8).permute(2, 4, 0, 1, 3, 5).reshape(m_padded, -1)
+    return y_fp4, y_sf
+

     inv_perm = torch.empty_like(perm)
     inv_perm[perm] = torch.arange(perm.numel(), device=perm.device, dtype=perm.dtype)

inline_comments.body: [BBuf Review Agent] Qwen3 NVFP4 with `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin` now sends an FP4 tuple to `apply_fp4_marlin_linear`, which requires a floating-point tensor, so the first forward crashes. Could we exclude Marlin in the shared enabling check and cover this MLP handoff?

@BBuf 
Thanks!
On SM80-SM90 `auto` also picks Marlin, so this would have broken the default path there. f5c2129d keeps the fusion off on the Marlin backend. Qwen3.5's dense MLP uses the same check, so it's covered too, and `test_stays_off_for_the_marlin_backend` fails without the change.

Checked with Qwen3-Reranker NVFP4 checkpoints:
- L4 (SM89, `auto` picks Marlin): the previous head failed on the first forward. Greedy outputs and logprobs now match main exactly (0.6B and 4B).
- RTX PRO 6000 with `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`: the previous head failed with `'tuple' object has no attribute 'dtype'`. It now serves normally.
- RTX PRO 6000 with the default backend: the fusion stays on, and outputs match main exactly.

While re-checking the handoff I found one more case. When down_proj's K is not a multiple of 64, the FP4 scales are padded, and the fused kernel leaves the padding unwritten (fp4_quantize zeroes it). In a kernel test with K = 1376 and 608, a NaN byte left there turned the whole GEMM output into NaN. 47dcb3e4 keeps the fusion off for such K; every Qwen3 size at TP <= 8 is a multiple of 64. 8b512342 moves the kill switch into `Envs` and logs the enable message once.
[BBuf Review Agent] The shared guard now excludes Marlin for both Qwen3 and Qwen3.5, and the regression test covers that check. This addresses the tuple handoff crash.
